title: Check your understanding: Recovering Lost Commits

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of recovering lost commits?
options: Recovery and maintenance depend on retaining evidence before cleanup. Reflogs and unreachable objects may provide recovery leads, while tested backups are more dependable than an assumption that recovery will always be possible.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Recovery and maintenance depend on retaining evidence before cleanup. Reflogs and unreachable objects may provide recovery leads, while tested backups are more dependable than an assumption that recovery will always be possible.
questions.explanation: Recovery and maintenance depend on retaining evidence before cleanup. Reflogs and unreachable objects may provide recovery leads, while tested backups are more dependable than an assumption that recovery will always be possible.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git reflog --date=relative -10` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with recovering lost commits?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
